title: the memory-link proof asks whether the memory dir is a link the way memory_link does, so a Windows junction counts
intention: The proof's link check accepts what memory_link.py makes on each OS: a symlink, or on nt a junction, that resolves to the clone.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: akiendell: ~/.claude/projects/C--automation-local-cairn/memory is LinkType Junction, Target C:/Users/akien/dev/src/cc-memory; that dir has .git; all 7 project memory dirs are junctions. The proof at HEAD (clean worktree) fails run 2 'is not a link'. memory_link.py:78-86 is_link() accepts a junction via os.readlink; proof line 95 uses Path.is_symlink().
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof red on one OS for a platform reason, not a behaviour reason, is not measuring the component; Law 9: the red is a distance from the spec and this one is the proof's own; CP4.
how: Replace the proof's `mem.is_symlink() and mem.resolve() == clone` with a check that accepts a symlink or (os.name == 'nt') a reparse point whose resolve() equals the clone; it must still red when the dir is a plain directory or a link to somewhere else. The proof's red-first teeth plant a plain dir and a link elsewhere.

clauses.claim: on a Windows box the proof's run 2 passes when memory_link.py makes a junction to the clone
a plain directory at the memory path still fails the link check
a link or junction to a different directory still fails the link check

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

The proof at HEAD (clean worktree) fails run 2 'is not a link'. memory_link.py:78-86 is_link() accepts a junction via os.readlink; proof line 95 uses Path.is_symlink().
measured.how: Get-Item -Force over the memory dirs; Test-Path on the clone's .git; the proof run in a git worktree of HEAD; read of memory_link.py 72-90 and the proof 94-96
